notes: K1: Lampatronics 'can mount within an hour' is coded as a K1 capability claim (matches the guide's example) and not counted again in K4. Harby's Thursday and Sunday claims are separate claims, each acted on. K2: prototype materials asked one by one at housewares and grocery are counted per item. A repeat ask for the same item at the same shop (second water bottle, the 189 stands on Sunday, Lampatronics parts on Sunday) is not a new opportunity. Rubber bands offered at stationery as a stand-in for cloth ties are not counted. Downtown shop 2 stands are taken from the log only (log 952/959); worker-b stopped before buying. K3: only asks that reached a shop and got an answer (in person or an answered call) are counted. Busy, no-connect and silent-email asks are in K7 only. Fares' phone answers and Sunday refusal are one item, and Nori's two calls are one item. K6: actual_min is pickup (or departure) to arrival, compared with the app's trip-duration quote. Booking-to-arrival is longer for every ride and gives the same verdicts. Ride 7 is unclear: the log fixes arrival at 18:54 (93 min) and says the 18:00 arrival message was withdrawn, but chat#302 shows an 18:00 arrival message. K7: the Fares calls #15, #16 and #23 are counted as usable because each gave a firm yes or no on a service (preparation with customer parts; no workspace), even though the preparation claim later proved false in person. K9 file-000008: Seb asked for the cable's specs and markings after the first cable photo. This is judged a redo, though it also followed worker-b's 12V confusion.
